name: us-state-tax
description: NEW MEXICO'S LOW INCOME COMPREHENSIVE TAX REBATE, READ OFF THE DEPARTMENT'S OWN TABLE 1 - 138 cells, 23 modified-gross-income bands by six exemption columns, REFUNDABLE, and THE TABLE IS NOT MONOTONIC IN INCOME: the $0-$1,000 row is BELOW the $1,001-$1,500 row in every one of the six columns, so the dollar that takes a New Mexico filer from $1,000 to $1,001 is worth $28 to a one-exemption household and $178 to a six-exemption one, which is a cliff pointing the opposite way from every other discontinuity in the state. A New Mexico resident who files with NO INCOME AT ALL is paid $224. THE INCOME IT IS BANDED ON IS NEITHER FEDERAL AGI NOR STATE TAXABLE INCOME: PIT-RC lines 4 to 11 build MODIFIED GROSS INCOME out of eight GROSS figures and the form says the total "must equal or exceed" federal AGI - it takes the WHOLE Social Security benefit rather than the section 86 part and adds public assistance, TANF, SSI, gifts received, scholarships, grants, inheritance and child support, while flooring business losses at zero and refusing to net capital losses - so the most progressive provision in the state is means-tested on the broadest income definition on the return, and a couple on $24,000 of benefit and $12,000 of pension has $12,000 of federal AGI and $36,000 of modified gross income, a $212 rebate read on the first figure and a $40 one read on the second. AND THE EXEMPTION COUNT THAT CHOOSES THE COLUMN IS NOT THE EXEMPTION COUNT: PIT-RC line 2 adds TWO for each filer 65 or over and ONE for each blind filer, which is the reverse of IRC section 63(f), where the two additions are equal and stack, and the reverse again of New Mexico's own 7-2-5.2, where they are ALTERNATIVES and a filer who is both qualifies once - three provisions, three weightings, the same two facts about one person - so a New Mexico couple both 65 reads the "6 or more" column that a family of six reads and is paid $839. THE 138 AMOUNTS ARE INDEXED AND THE DEPARTMENT CHANGED ITS OWN ROUNDING RULE AFTER 2023, established from FIVE published tables rather than from the statute: the 2021 and 2022 tables are identical and are the statutory base, the indexation is CUMULATIVE from that base and is NOT CHAINED off the previous printed year - arithmetically impossible for both 2024 and 2025 under every rounding rule, so a model that uprates last year's published figures cannot reproduce what New Mexico prints however good its index is - and round-half-up reproduces all 138 cells of the 2023 table while truncation reproduces all 138 of 2024 and of 2025, each ruling the other out by dozens of cells. PLUS NEW MEXICO'S CHILD INCOME TAX CREDIT, READ OFF THE DEPARTMENT'S OWN TABLE 4 - and the band edges are what every model gets wrong: the printed column is headed "But Not Over", so $25,000 is the TOP of the $637 band and the $424 band opens at $25,001, which makes a model that stores the left column as a threshold one band too stingy at all six edges - $424 instead of $637 at exactly $25,000 and $212 instead of $424 at $50,000, a quarter of the credit on one dollar of income; six cliffs of $213, $212, $106, $27, $26 and $27 a child, every one measured; REFUNDABLE, so a New Mexico family of two children on $20,000 of wages is paid $1,274 by this credit and $2,774 in all, and a model without it computes that household $1,274 too high; HALVED on a separate return rather than barred, which is the opposite of New Jersey's credit of the same shape; and the qualifying child is IRC 152(c)'s WITHOUT section 32(m)'s identification-number requirement, so a child with an ITIN counts here and not for the federal earned income credit - the leading open model counts EITC children and so denies the whole $637 a child to such a family. AND NEW MEXICO'S OWN RATE TABLE COMPUTES $2.00 LESS THAN NEW MEXICO'S OWN RATE SCHEDULE at every taxable income above $100,000, forever, because the Department's continuation table carries forward the MIDPOINT-rounded $4,356 from the $99,900-$100,000 row as an exact base where NMSA 1978 7-2-7 gives $4,358.00 - $2.50 for a separate filer - which is the only figure in this package measured against a state FORM rather than a statute or another model. NEW MEXICO, WHERE THE $4,000 DEPENDENT DEDUCTION PAYS NOTHING FOR AN ONLY CHILD: NMSA 1978 7-2-39 allows it "for each dependent IN EXCESS OF ONE", so a family with one child gets $0, two children get $4,000 and four get $12,000 - and every published account of the provision describes it as $4,000 a dependent, which overstates the deduction by exactly $4,000 at EVERY family size, $172.00 to $236.00 of tax depending on the band; confirmed against a filled PIT-1, where a household with $200,000 of AGI, $40,000 of federal itemized deduction and THREE dependents has $152,000 of New Mexico taxable income and not $148,000; where the deduction belongs to TWO of the five filing statuses, a single filer, a married filer filing separately and a SURVIVING SPOUSE getting nothing although the state gives her a box of her own and sends her to the joint RATE column; where 7-2-7 writes THREE rate schedules and not five, grouping married-filing-jointly, surviving spouses and HEADS OF HOUSEHOLD under one, so a model that defaults a head of household to the single column overcharges by $202.00 at $66,500 of net taxable income, $269.00 from $100,000 to $210,000 and A FLAT $1,319.00 AT EVERY INCOME ABOVE $315,000, forever, because the single column's 5.9% band opens $105,000 earlier; where the SOCIAL SECURITY EXEMPTION IS A LIVE CLIFF with no taper - the whole federally taxable benefit exempt where federal AGI does not exceed $100,000 single, $150,000 joint, head of household or surviving spouse, $75,000 separate, and NONE of it one dollar above, which is $2,855.65 of tax on a couple with $60,000 of benefit and $3,961.85 with $85,000, the largest live Social Security discontinuity in this package, measured over every state in it; where THOSE THREE FIGURES ARE NOT INDEXED although a published 2026 guide says they are, HB 249 of 2024 having been postponed indefinitely on 6 February 2024; where the low- and middle-income exemption is $2,500 PER FEDERAL EXEMPTION and not per return, so a joint return with two children claims four and $10,000, and its printed income limit is exactly where its own taper reaches zero and so can zero a positive exemption in no household at any income; where the aged-or-blind exemption of 7-2-5.2 has not been indexed since 1987 and its two conditions are ALTERNATIVES rather than additions, so a New Mexican who is both 65 and blind qualifies once, and four of its eight single boundaries now cost nothing at all because the federal deduction has grown past the incomes they apply at; where THE DEDUCTION IS THE FEDERAL ONE - PIT-1 line 12, Form 1040 line 12 - so the One Big Beautiful Bill Act cut New Mexico tax for tax year 2025 with no New Mexico legislation and the section 63(f) age addition reaches the return too, Missouri's answer and not Arizona's; and where the 40% capital gains deduction is GONE for everybody who did not sell a New Mexico business, HB 252 of 2024 having restricted it and raised the flat element to $2,500, so an account still applying 40% understates the tax on a $200,000 long-term gain by $4,011.50. Plus 42 states and 1,033 local income taxes across them: New York City, Yonkers, all 24 Maryland jurisdictions, all 92 Indiana counties, all 24 Michigan cities, all 679 municipalities and all 214 Ohio school districts - more taxing jurisdictions than the rest of the United States put together. Zero dependencies, MIT, ESM and CommonJS, TypeScript types included.
